predictions.selection: Milwaukee Brewers to win Game 2 of the World Series (moneyline).
predictions.text: Milwaukee opened the Series with a win and now sends Logan Henderson to the mound at American Family Field, where the Brewers went 55-26 during the regular season. Their 103-59 record was the best in the National League, they scored 832 runs against 618 allowed for a plus-214 differential, and they closed the regular season 8-2 in their last ten, according to MLB's official standings. Tampa Bay finished 98-64 but was a far more ordinary 43-38 on the road. Henderson against Drew Rasmussen is the pitching matchup MLB lists for this game. No injury designation for either club could be read from an official source before publication.

predictions.match: Los Angeles Kings @ New Jersey Devils
predictions.selection: New Jersey Devils to beat the Los Angeles Kings in regulation or beyond (moneyline).
predictions.text: New Jersey is 6-4-0 through ten games with a plus-two goal difference and is at home, where the club has been far the steadier side. Los Angeles has played only eight games but arrives at 2-4-2 with 20 goals scored and 29 conceded, the thinnest offensive record on tonight's board. The Devils' 21.9 per cent power play against a Kings penalty kill that has been ordinary is the likeliest route to separation. The best price on the league's own feed is -192, shorter than the -154 we make them, so this is a form call and not a value call: back the Devils to win, but accept that the market has most of the edge already priced in.

predictions.selection: Boston Bruins to beat the San Jose Sharks (moneyline).
predictions.text: Boston is 8-2-1 with two shutouts and has conceded only 22 goals in 11 games, the best defensive record of any club on tonight's slate. San Jose is 6-4-1 but has been outscored 36-32 and has won just one game in regulation. The Bruins' 80.6 per cent penalty kill against a Sharks power play converting 25.7 per cent is the matchup that matters most, and Boston's home form has been the foundation of its start. The league feed lists the Bruins at -182 against our -162, which is a fair reflection of the gap and leaves thin margin for a buyer.

predictions.match: Vegas Golden Knights @ Columbus Blue Jackets
predictions.selection: Vegas Golden Knights to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets (moneyline).
predictions.text: Vegas is 8-4-0 with 45 goals for and has won seven of its last ten, while Columbus is 3-5-0 with only 19 goals in eight games and the weakest power play on tonight's card at 8.7 per cent. The Blue Jackets have also lost five of six, and their minus-ten goal difference is the second-worst of any home side playing today. The feed quotes Vegas at -132 where we make them -126, a small disagreement that still favours the visitor.

predictions.selection: Ottawa Senators to beat the New York Rangers (moneyline).
predictions.text: Ottawa is 7-4-0 and has conceded only 30 goals in 11 games, while the Rangers have played 12 games for 15 points and have been outshot in several of them. The Senators' 2-0 record in games decided beyond regulation and their home ice tilt a close matchup. Both sides sit on 14 points, so this is close to a coin flip and the market agrees; the best published price for Ottawa on the league's own list is -109 (feed 6). Our line gives Ottawa 52.8 per cent, so no edge is claimed either way.

predictions.selection: Pittsburgh Penguins to beat the Nashville Predators (moneyline).
predictions.text: Nashville has three overtime defeats in nine games and has scored only 23 goals, the lowest total of any club playing tonight. Pittsburgh's own start is poor at 4-6-1, but the Penguins have generated 36 goals and put 30 shots a game on opposing nets, and they are at home. Nashville is only a narrow favourite at +105 on the league's price feed, so a Penguins win at plus money is the largest disagreement between our line and the published market on this slate.

predictions.selection: Washington Capitals to beat the Buffalo Sabres (moneyline).
predictions.text: Washington has squeezed ten points from nine games despite a modest goal difference, and Buffalo has conceded 36 goals in ten, the second-worst rate among tonight's twelve hosts and visitors. The Sabres have also lost both of their overtime decisions, a sign of thin margins late in games. Washington's .556 points percentage is built on five regulation wins in nine, and the club is at home. The feed asks only -102 for Washington while we make them -131, and that gap is the widest value edge on the card: Capitals to win is the bet.
